dominant_strengths: Confident editorial typography pairing oversized headline with muted descender clause creates clear semantic hierarchy
Logo strip executes the social-proof pattern cleanly with consistent grayscale weight and even rhythmic spacing
Product mock cards show genuine craft: realistic checkout, device chrome, and gradient artifacts feel native to Stripe
dominant_weaknesses: Vivid magenta/orange gradient blob in hero competes with content density and feels disconnected from the cooler card region below
Two feature cards sit awkwardly against a near-white background with weak containment, making the section feel floaty rather than gridded
CTA pair mixes a saturated indigo button with a Google-branded button, creating visual weight imbalance and brand dilution
fix_priorities: Tame or crop the hero gradient so it doesn't bleed past the logo strip and visually separate from the cards section
Add subtle card surfaces, borders, or a structured background to anchor the feature cards in a clearer grid
Rebalance CTA hierarchy—reduce Google button prominence or unify with a tertiary outline treatment
Tighten vertical rhythm between hero, logo strip, and section heading; current gaps read inconsistent
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral pull from the gradient and clean type, solid behavioral clarity in feature framing, but reflective payoff is generic Stripe-template territory.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—this reads convincingly as a Stripe scroll section with appropriate fintech polish, even if it doesn't push beyond the established Stripe visual language.
